# Agentdock

Agentdock connects a compiled LangGraph agent to an application through a
canonical event contract and streaming transports. LangChain and LangGraph own
execution, models, tools, checkpoints, interrupts, and resume. Applications own
routes, requests, authentication, authorization, thread identity, context, side
effects, providers, and saver lifecycle.

## Install and serve

Requires Node.js 22+ and LangGraph 1.4.17+.

npm install @agentdock-ai/agentdock @agentdock-ai/contracts @langchain/core @langchain/langgraph langchain zod

Install the chosen provider integration separately, for example @langchain/openrouter.

```ts
import { Agentdock } from "@agentdock-ai/agentdock";
import { ChatOpenRouter } from "@langchain/openrouter";
import { MemorySaver } from "@langchain/langgraph";
import { createAgent } from "langchain";

const graph = createAgent({
  model: new ChatOpenRouter({ model: "openai/gpt-4o-mini" }),
  tools: [],
  checkpointer: new MemorySaver(),
}).graph;
const runtime = new Agentdock(graph);
await runtime.pipe(response, {
  threadId: authorizedThreadId,
  input: { messages: [{ role: "user", content: prompt }] },
  context: trustedContext,
});
```

No Agentdock state schema is required. Agentdock reads native pending tasks and
never writes event bookkeeping into graph state. MemorySaver is for development;
use a durable LangGraph saver in production and manage its lifecycle in the app.

## API

- new Agentdock(graph, options?) creates a runtime.
- Options: recursionLimit override; interruptFormat (Agentdock.OPAQUE by default
  or Agentdock.HITL for LangChain HITL presentation; equivalent strings remain
  supported); validateResume preflight hook; onError server diagnostics.
- runtime.stream(run) returns an async iterable of canonical contract events.
- runtime.pipe(nodeResponse, run) writes SSE with backpressure and disconnect cancellation.
- runtime.toResponse(run) returns a promise for a cancelable Web Response.
- runtime.getMessages(threadId, { channel?, config? }?) reads native checkpoint messages.
- runtime.getResumeState(threadId, config?) projects pending native control state,
  or returns null; invalid projections throw. A seed has runId: null.
- Starts: { threadId, input }. Dynamic resumes: { threadId, resume }.
  Static continuations: { threadId, continue: true }.
- Every form accepts optional context, signal, and config. Config forwards native
  callbacks, tags, metadata, store, and extra configurable values. Serving controls
  stream modes and overwrites configurable.thread_id with the authorized thread.
- Contract types, reducers, and validators come from @agentdock-ai/contracts,
  not from the core package.
- Every invocation has a fresh runId and sequence starting at 1.

## Interrupt and resume

Use LangChain humanInTheLoopMiddleware or native LangGraph interrupts with a
checkpointer. For LangChain approval presentation, construct Agentdock with
interruptFormat: "langchain-hitl". The optional validateToolApprovalResume helper
checks the response envelope/action count, not authority.

Listen for interrupt.required and authorize the user before continuation.

```ts
await runtime.pipe(response, {
  threadId: authorizedThreadId,
  context: trustedContext,
  resume: { decisions: [{ type: "approve" }] },
});
```

Target native interrupt IDs for multiple pending interrupts:
resume: { [interruptId]: { decisions: [{ type: "approve" }] } }.
A static breakpoint emits run.paused; continue it with continue: true.
Hydrate pending control state with getResumeState and load history separately.

## Agentdock UI

Agentdock UI adds a chat interface to your Agentdock application. The published
CLI copies small, editable components into components/agentdock-ui. The
@agentdock-ai/react npm package provides the store, hooks, event decoding, and
render model. Your application owns network requests and authentication.

The UI supports streaming, Markdown, tools, approvals, cancellation, saved history,
and optional files/images. It inherits host shadcn semantic tokens and supports
Radix or Base UI. Requires Node.js 22+, React 18+, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, a resolvable
TypeScript alias, and shadcn semantic theme tokens.

From your React application's directory, install the chat with:

npx @agentdock-ai/agentdock-ui add chat

The installer detects npm, pnpm, Yarn, or Bun, checks required dependencies and
versions, and installs missing dependencies with the detected package manager.
It copies the appropriate Radix or Base UI source into the app. An existing
components.json selects the primitive set; if missing, the installer can create
it using the detected alias and theme. Use --cwd ./apps/web to target an app in
a monorepo, or --dry-run to preview without writing files or installing packages.
Repeated installs preserve edited source; --overwrite explicitly replaces it.
The Starter provides npm run ui:add to refresh its chat components.

For a custom interface, install the runtime package with your app's package
manager. With npm, run: npm install @agentdock-ai/react react. The editable Chat
source is copied into your project; it is not imported as a prebuilt component
package.

```tsx
import { Chat } from "@/components/agentdock-ui/chat";
<Chat adapter={appOwnedChatAdapter} />;
```

Hydrate normalized history and optional native resume state into a fresh AgentStore
before streaming. See https://agentdock-ai.vercel.app/docs/ui.

The UI guide also includes a component catalog with representative previews for
the conversation, composer, activity, layout, and control building blocks. The
previews use sample content and do not connect to an agent.
